babadab33ae53473.label: MAKE
babadab33ae53473.summary: Satellite radar imaging uncovers a massive 2,600-year-old administrative and temple complex buried under 20 feet of Nile delta silt. Hook: 'Satellites orbiting 400 miles above Earth just found a massive lost Egyptian city hidden under 20 feet of Nile mud.'
babadab33ae53473.notes:
- Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and multispectral satellite sensors penetrated alluvial mud deposits
- Revealed an immense 2,600-year-old Saite/Persian-period military and temple complex previously undocumented in historical records
- Highlights how orbital satellite archaeology is discovering buried civilizational ruins without invasive digging

3c104026871d31ec.label: MAKE
3c104026871d31ec.summary: Ancient Roman artisans milled colloidal gold and silver to 70 nanometers to create the Lycurgus Cup, which changes color in transmitted light. Hook: '1,600 years ago, Roman glassmakers accidentally invented nanotechnology—and scientists only figured out how in 1990.'
3c104026871d31ec.notes:
- 4th-century Roman dichroic glass goblet depicting King Lycurgus
- Exhibits plasmonic color shifts: opaque green under external reflected light, glowing translucent red when lit from within
- British Museum electron microscopy revealed Roman artisans embedded 70nm gold-silver alloy nanoparticles centuries before modern physics existed

f68b0765bc10726f.notes:
- High-energy astrophysical neutrinos detected via Cherenkov radiation across one cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice
- Pinpoints blazar relativistic particle acceleration outside the Milky Way
